title: Picks: a chain pick on a .sc model follows by the pair of SolidCraft face names when the model imports again
body:
Part of #3915. Uses #4212 and #4213.

**What happens now**
- A chain pick (an edge, or a loop of edges) is also a geometry hash. In the baseline (#3915), 10 of 19 chains were lost after the 60 → 80 mm change.
- One lost chain is the end edge of the top face, the kind of edge that a profile cut follows. Generate refused the 2D Contour on it: "Edge of 'part' is no longer in the model: re-pick it".
- The SolidCraft cache names faces only, not edges. But SolidCraft already uses a pair of face names for an edge: the fillet on the edge between `F2:side:b` and `F2:side:c` is the face `F3:blend(F2:side:b|F2:side:c)`. The lost edge above lies between `F2:side:a` and `F2:bottom`, and both names are in the 80 mm file.

**Need**
- When a `.sc` model imports again, a chain pick on it follows by the pair of SolidCraft face names of each edge.
- A chain that is the whole loop of one face can follow that face.
- The rules of #4213 apply: exactly one candidate, only `verified` names, a visible follow, and a pick that cannot follow is named in the re-import report and refused at generate as today.
- The path kernel (#4023; K1 is #4025) turns each pick into a `Chain` and takes geometry, not pick ids. A chain that follows is a normal pick id, so the path kernel needs no change for this.

**Done means**
- On the fixtures of #4212 and #4213:
  - a chain pick on an edge between two named faces follows after a design change;
  - a chain whose face pair is gone, or is not unique, does not follow: the re-import report names it, and generate refuses it as today.
- A model with no names behaves as today.

I prepared this issue with Claude Code (an AI agent) and checked it.

title: MCP: show the SolidCraft face names of a .sc model, and name the followed and lost picks after a re-import
body:
Part of #3915. Uses #4212 and #4213.

**What happens now**
- An agent picks faces through MCP by their ids. `list_features` and `get_operation_geometry` give the ids, but not the SolidCraft names.
- After a re-import, the `import_model` answer gives the facet count only (baseline in #3915). An agent cannot see which picks were lost.

**Need**
- `list_features` and `get_operation_geometry` give the SolidCraft name (or names) of each face and patch that has one. These are new JSON fields. The fields that exist now do not change.
- After a re-import, the `import_model` answer names each pick that followed and each pick that could not follow (#4213).

**Fit with #3814**
- #3814 asks for the change summary in the `import_model` answer: the counts of carried, added and missing faces, patches and chains. It is open, with no PR.
- This sub-issue adds names to that summary. It can fold into #3814, or come after #3814 and add to its summary. You decide.

**Done means**
- A headless MCP test on a `.sc` fixture: `list_features` and `get_operation_geometry` give the names. A model with no names gives none, and its answer is the same as today.
- After a re-import, `import_model` names each followed pick and each pick that could not follow.

I prepared this issue with Claude Code (an AI agent) and checked it.

title: Picks: a face pick on a .sc model follows its face by the SolidCraft name when the model imports again
body:
Part of #3915. Uses #4212.

**What happens now**
- A face pick is a hash of the face geometry (`crates/geometry/src/geometry/feature.rs:884`). When a design change moves the face or changes its size, the id is gone, and generate refuses the pick: "Face of 'part' is no longer in the model: re-pick it".
- Baseline on 0.27.0 (https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3915#issuecomment-7201006498): the bracket at 60 mm, then 80 mm. The features of 8 of the 11 SolidCraft faces were lost, and generate refused the operations on them. The 80 mm file holds the same 11 names.
- CamCraft does not guess that a missing face and an added face are the same face: "re-picking is Stage C's decision, made visible to the user, never assumed" (`crates/geometry/src/geometry/revision.rs:17-20`). A SolidCraft name is not a guess. It is SolidCraft's own identity for the face. But the follow must be visible (Q2).

**Need**
- When a `.sc` model imports again, a face pick on it follows its face by its SolidCraft name.
- A pick that cannot follow is named in the re-import report, and generate refuses it as today.
- The geometry still decides. A pick follows only when exactly one new face has the same name set and the same kind (plane, or not a plane).
  - A CamCraft face or patch over several SolidCraft faces has a set of names.
  - A new face whose `former` is equal to an old name counts as a face with that name.
  - A name that is not `verified`: no follow.
- A pick whose id is still in the model does not change.
- Scope: the picks that operations hold (the geometry selection, area picks, "Do not touch" picks, and the pick stores of each kind). Setup, WCS, alignment, fixture and electrode picks behave as today. Start and exit picks are coordinates, not feature ids, so they behave as today.
- The follow also works when the project was saved and opened again, or runs headless, before the new revision arrives.
- The re-import and the follows are one undo step.
- A model with no names behaves as today.

**Questions for the maintainer**
- **Q1. A `PROJECT_VERSION` step?** The follow in a reopened project needs data from the earlier import, so the solution can save data in the project file. If it does, does that data need a version step?
  - `solids` (#917) has no step: "an old reader that drops it reads the soup" (`crates/app/src/project/entity.rs:637-644`).
  - `source` (#2463) came with v72: "An old reader must refuse a v72 file" (`crates/app/src/project/source_dto.rs:1-5`).
  - Recommended: no step. An old reader that drops the data gives today's behaviour, as with `solids`. A step also lands only at a cut, and older builds then refuse each file that the new build saves.
- **Q2. Follow automatically, or offer the follow?**
  - Follow at re-import, and add a needs-review line to each operation that has a followed pick; or
  - offer the follows as one step that the user or the agent accepts.
  - Recommended: follow, with a needs-review line that names the face, for example "face 'F2:side:b' of 'part' followed by its SolidCraft name after the model was imported again". It is one undo step, it is visible, and `mark_operation_reviewed` clears it (`crates/app/src/mcp/order_tools.rs:24`). Today the `needs_review` field of an operation (`crates/app/src/project/entity.rs:442`) holds migration warnings; this is a second use.
- **Q3. Do `Patch` picks follow in this sub-issue?**
  - Recommended: yes, by name set.
  - 2D Pocket takes a patch pick. In the baseline, the bracket's patch over three SolidCraft faces has the same name set in both files.

**Done means**
- Two revisions of one design, with the same names in a different order (fixtures as Q4 in #4212 decides):
  - a face pick on a face that moved or changed size follows by its name;
  - a `Patch` pick follows by its name set (if Q3 is yes);
  - a pick on a removed face does not follow: the re-import report names it, and generate refuses it as today;
  - an unverified name, two candidates, or a change of kind: no follow;
  - a `former` name follows;
  - each operation with a followed pick shows the follow (as Q2 decides);
  - undo puts back the old picks, and redo makes the follow again;
  - import, save, open, then import again: the follow works.
- STL, OBJ, STEP and a `.sc` with no names: the same behaviour as today.

I prepared this issue with Claude Code (an AI agent) and checked it.

title: Import: keep the SolidCraft source face and its name for each facet of a .sc model
body:
Part of #3915.

**What happens now**
- A `.sc` model comes from one SolidCraft body. The kernel knows the record face of each triangle (`MachiningMesh::tri_face`, `crates/kernel/src/machining_mesh.rs:46`).
- The import drops it. `push_facets` copies only the three corners (`crates/geometry/src/kernel_import.rs:13-26`).
- The `.sc` reader does not read the face names.
- SolidCraft writes one name for each face of the body record, in record order, in `cache/model.json` at `model.names[n].faces`. Each face also has `info`: `[aliases, bounds, verified, synonyms]`, and from SolidCraft 0.50.0 an optional fifth item, `former`. The research comments in #3915 give the sources and the runs.

**Need**
- After a `.sc` import, CamCraft knows for each facet its source face and the SolidCraft name of that face, with its `verified` flag and its `former` name.
- The import never fails because of names. Name data with a wrong count, a wrong shape or a value out of bounds gives no names, and the import continues as today.
- When the facets change by a different route (for example `repair_model`), the names must not stay on the wrong facets.
- STL, OBJ, STEP and a `.sc` file with no names: no names.
- A user sees no change in behaviour from this sub-issue. The other sub-issues of #3915 (picks, MCP) use the names.

**Questions for the maintainer**
- **Q5. Names from cache format 10 only?**
  - Format 10 is the format of SolidCraft's published names writer (`crates/doc/src/model_cache.rs`).
  - CamCraft knows format 8 only from the sample `testdata/models/solidcraft_for_beginners.sc` (`crates/kernel/src/solidcraft/mod.rs:51-53`), and the reader takes no layout from sample bytes (`mod.rs:15`).
  - Recommended: format 10 only. A format-8 model imports as today, with no names.
- **Q4. Which fixtures?** The options:
  - containers that the tests build in code, with names of our own, as `crates/kernel/tests/solidcraft_import/` already does;
  - `testdata/models/hole_on_pocket_wall.sc` (cache format 10, with names);
  - a pair that SolidCraft made from its `examples/bracket.json`, at `width` 60 mm and 80 mm.
  - Recommended: the containers that the tests build, first. Also `hole_on_pocket_wall.sc` if your rule on SolidCraft material permits it. The SolidCraft-made pair only with your permission.
  - The same choice applies to the tests of the other sub-issues.

**Done means**
- After a `.sc` import (cache format 10), each facet has its source face, and the SolidCraft name, `verified` flag and `former` name of that face. `info` with four items and with five items both read.
- A test shows that each facet gets the name of the face that it lies on, not only the correct count of names. (Facets that shift by one also give the correct count.)
- Bad name data gives no names, and the import is OK. The hostile-input tests cover the names part with no panic.
- STL, OBJ, STEP, a format-8 `.sc` and a `.sc` with no names: no names, and the behaviour is the same as today.

I prepared this issue with Claude Code (an AI agent) and checked it.

title: UI: the viewport line colours (plain [f32; 3] consts) read the theme's token table
body:
Follow-up of #1120 (found during the #1120 family PRs #3990, #3992, #3993, #4072, #4073, #4207 and #4208).

## What is there now

After #4208, each `Color32` literal at a draw site in `crates/ui/src` reads a theme token, and the colour-literal guard (`crates/ui/tests/theme_files/colour_literals.rs`) has only permanent rows. The guard counts `Color32` literals only. About 19 viewport line colours are plain-number `[f32; 3]` (or `[u8; 3]`) constants, and the guard cannot see them:

- `crates/ui/src/interact.rs`: `VIEWPORT_BG`, `GRID_MINOR`, `GRID_MAJOR`, `REGION_RGB`, `CLEARANCE_RGB`, `RETRACT_RGB`, `CUT_RGB`, `PICK_RGB` (the move kinds `FEED_RGB`, `RAPID_RGB` and `PLUNGE_RGB` are in the verdict palettes of #4207 and stay ours).
- `crates/ui/src/sketch_overlay.rs`: `SKETCH_RGB`, `OPEN_END_RGB`.
- `crates/ui/src/work_envelope.rs`: `ENVELOPE_RGB`.
- `crates/ui/src/boundary_viz.rs`: `HOVER_RGB`.
- `crates/ui/src/align_pick_viz.rs`: `PICK_RGB8` (the same violet as `PICK_RGB`, in 0..255).
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/colorvision.rs`: `EDGE_DARK`, `EDGE_WIRE`; `crates/ui/src/egui_app/ground_ink.rs`: `EDGE_WIRE_LIGHT` and the light-ground arms of `overlay_ink` (#698).

Most of these go to the shaders or to the overlay vertex colours. Several have a dark set and a light-ground set (#698), selected by the luminance of the viewport ground.

## Why it is a separate issue

#1120 counted the `Color32` sites (its estimate said 51). These constants are a different design:

- They are display sRGB floats for the GPU, not `Color32`.
- A ground-dependent pair needs the ground rule of #3993 (a theme key that is not set follows the ground when it flips).
- Some (`VIEWPORT_BG`, the grid) may be older copies of the `viewport` token and could be removed, not moved.
- `EDGE_DARK` and `EDGE_WIRE` are inputs of the colour-vision gate, so they may stay ours like the verdict palettes.

## Done means

- Each constant above is either a theme token (`Tokens` field, both columns with the old value, a theme-file key) or a named row of a table that stays ours, with the reason in a decision record.
- A guard (an extension of `colour_scan`, or a second scan) refuses a new plain-number colour array outside the token tables.
- Each colour renders the same as before in the dark and light theme, on both viewport grounds and in each colour-vision mode (asserted on the values; no snapshot PNG touched).

Suggested labels (I cannot set labels): `enhancement`, `area:ui`, `P6`, `effort:medium`.

title: 2D Contour: add integrated finish and spring passes

labels.name: needs-research
labels.description: Large idea with open questions: research and file sub-issues before any code

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
## Problem

2D Contour can leave stock for a later finishing operation.

A user must currently create and maintain another Contour operation to remove that stock. A spring pass needs another duplicated operation.

The duplicated operation repeats the geometry, lead settings, start point, exit point, heights, tabs and tool selection. A later change can make the rough and finish operations disagree.

## Proposal

Add an optional finish sequence to the 2D Contour operation.

The operator can create the complete rough and finish sequence in one operation. CamCraft keeps the current behavior when the option is off.

Add these controls to the Passes tab:

- `Stock to leave`
- `Finish in this operation`
- `Finish allowance`
- `Finishing passes`
- `Spring passes`

The proposed layout is:

```text
Stock to leave                 0.00 mm

☐ Finish in this operation
    Finish allowance           0.25 mm
    Finishing passes           1
    Spring passes              0
```

CamCraft hides the finish fields while `Finish in this operation` is off.

## Meaning of the values

`Stock to leave` remains the material that the complete operation leaves on the final wall.

`Finish allowance` is the additional material that the finishing passes remove.

`Finishing passes` divides the finish allowance across the finishing passes.

`Spring passes` repeats the final path without a new planned allowance.

Let:

- `S` be `Stock to leave`.
- `A` be `Finish allowance`.
- `N` be `Finishing passes`.

The rough pass uses this offset from the final wall:

```text
S + A
```

Finishing pass `i` uses this offset:

```text
S + A × (N - i) / N
```

The final finishing pass stands exactly at `S`.

Every spring pass also stands at `S`.

### Example

Use these values:

- `Stock to leave = 0.00 mm`
- `Finish allowance = 0.30 mm`
- `Finishing passes = 2`
- `Spring passes = 1`

CamCraft generates:

1. A rough pass at 0.30 mm from the final wall.
2. A finishing pass at 0.15 mm from the final wall.
3. A finishing pass on the final wall.
4. A spring pass on the final wall.

CamCraft applies the same formula to Inside and Outside contours.

A positive `Stock to leave` remains on the final wall after the complete sequence. The finishing passes remove only the `Finish allowance`.

## Default values

A new 2D Contour keeps `Finish in this operation` off.

When the operator enables it, CamCraft starts with:

- `Finish allowance = 0.25 mm`
- `Finishing passes = 1`
- `Spring passes = 0`

A disabled finish sequence generates the current toolpath.

A zero finish allowance is valid. One finishing pass can then repeat the final contour at a separate finish feed.

The proposed limits are:

- Finishing passes: 1 to 64.
- Spring passes: 0 to 4.

## Finish feed

Add an optional finish-feed override to the Feeds tab.

The proposed layout is:

```text
Feed                           1200 mm/min
Plunge feed                     300 mm/min

☐ Override finish feed
    Finish feed                1200 mm/min
```

The override follows these rules:

- It starts off.
- It copies the current `Feed` when the operator enables it.
- It keeps the entered value until the operator disables it.
- It stops inheriting `Feed` while the override is enabled.
- It uses `Feed` dynamically while the override is disabled.
- It uses the new current `Feed` after the operator disables and enables it again.
- Finishing passes and spring passes use the effective finish feed.
- Rough passes use `Feed`.
- The operation stores no separate finish spindle speed.

The operator does not need a separate feed for every pass.

## Feed behavior

The finish sequence uses these feed rules:

- The wall cut uses `Feed` for rough passes.
- The wall cut uses `Finish feed` for finishing and spring passes.
- A lead-in uses its existing lead-in percentage of the active wall feed.
- A lead-out uses the active wall feed.
- Plunge, ramp, helix and explicit entry-feed settings keep their current behavior.
- An automatic entry feed reads the active rough or finish wall feed.
- The spindle speed remains the same for the complete operation.

The finish-feed override must not modify the selected tool or its recipe.

## Existing lead-in and lead-out

The feature does not add a second lead editor.

Every rough, finishing and spring pass uses the operation's existing lead-in, lead-out, extension, overlap and compensation settings.

Each pass follows this sequence:

```text
safe approach → lead-in → wall pass → lead-out → safe retract
```

CamCraft recalculates the lead geometry for every radial offset.

CamCraft applies the existing room, crossing and collision checks to every recalculated lead.

The path must not move directly from one wall offset to another wall offset.

CamCraft retracts between offsets. It then enters the next pass with a new lead.

If the configured lead does not fit, CamCraft uses the existing lead refusal or shortening behavior. It must not silently plunge through the finished wall.

A spring pass repeats the complete final sequence, including lead-in, wall pass, lead-out and retract.

## Pass order

CamCraft completes each offset as a separate Contour band.

For each selected contour:

1. Complete the rough depth ladder at the rough offset.
2. Retract to a safe plane.
3. Complete the first finishing depth ladder.
4. Retract to a safe plane.
5. Complete each remaining finishing depth ladder.
6. Retract to a safe plane.
7. Repeat the final depth ladder for each spring pass.

The operation completes all rings and Z levels of one offset before it starts the next offset.

The existing level links apply inside one offset.

A keep-down link must not cross from one offset to another. CamCraft must use a safe lift between offset bands.

The current start point, exit point, compensation mode, tabs, corner rounding, overlap and entry settings apply to every offset band.

Control and wear compensation engage and cancel independently for every rough, finishing and spring band.

CamCraft retains all generated spring passes. A post or path optimizer must not remove a repeated final pass as a duplicate.

## Open contours and multiple selections

The feature applies to:

- Closed Contour rings.
- Open model-edge chains.
- Open stock-source runs.
- Multiple selected rings.
- Multiple disconnected runs.
- Multiple Z levels.
- Tabbed Contours.
- Inside and Outside sides.
- Computer, Wear and Control compensation.

Each run receives an independent lead-in and lead-out for every offset.

## Collision and verification

CamCraft applies the complete existing verification rules to every pass.

This includes:

- Model collision checks.
- Full cutter-envelope checks.
- Stock checks.
- Flute, shank and holder checks.
- Lead-room checks.
- Lead crossing checks.
- Keep-down link checks.
- Tab checks.
- Compensation checks.
- Open-chain air-side checks.

A finishing or spring pass must block posting when any check fails.

CamCraft must not use a rough path result as proof for a different offset.

## Validation

CamCraft refuses the operation before geometry generation when:

- `Stock to leave + Finish allowance` is negative or not finite.
- `Finish allowance` is negative or not finite.
- `Finishing passes` is outside its allowed range.
- `Spring passes` is outside its allowed range.
- An enabled finish-feed override is not positive and finite.
- The initial rough offset produces no legal cutter-centre path.
- A selected ring collapses at a finish or spring offset.

CamCraft identifies the invalid field and value in the refusal.

CamCraft must propagate a later unsafe finish or spring pass as an operation failure. It must not return a partial clean path.

## Project format

Add an optional finish record to the 2D Contour parameters.

The record contains:

- Finish allowance.
- Finishing-pass count.
- Spring-pass count.

Add an optional finish-feed value.

An absent finish record means that the feature is off.

An absent finish-feed value means that finishing uses the current `Feed`.

Existing project files retain the current Contour behavior.

A project that enables the feature round-trips every value through save and load.

Older project data must not acquire extra passes through a default value.

## UI behavior

All changes use the existing undoable operation-parameter command.

The Passes tab enables and disables the finish fields.

The Feeds tab enables and disables the finish-feed field.

Turning on the feed override copies the current `Feed` into `Finish feed`.

Turning off the feed override clears the override and restores inheritance.

Opening either tab must not modify the operation.

## MCP behavior

Expose the finish sequence through the 2D Contour MCP fields.

The MCP update must support:

- Enabling and disabling the finish sequence.
- Finish allowance.
- Finishing-pass count.
- Spring-pass count.
- Enabling and disabling finish-feed inheritance.
- Explicit finish feed.

An absent finish record keeps the old one-pass behavior.

The MCP schema and generated documentation must list the fields.

## Scope

This issue covers 2D Contour only.

Later issues can reuse the same model for:

- Bore.
- Circular.
- Slot.
- Trochoidal Slot.
- Pocket.
- 2D Offset.
- 2D Adaptive.

Those operations need their own wall-finish path. A Pocket must not repeat its complete area-clearing path as a spring pass.

2D Chamfer remains separate because its passes move a tool cone across a chamfer width. That work is tracked by #3238.

This issue does not add:

- A separate spindle speed.
- A separate feed for every pass.
- A second lead editor.
- A different finish tool.
- Automatic tool changes.
- Floor finishing.
- A new 3D finishing pass system.

A separate finish operation remains valid when the job needs another tool, spindle speed or different entry strategy.

## Documentation

Update the 2D Contour operation guide.

Document:

- The Passes controls.
- The finish-allowance formula.
- The difference between finishing and spring passes.
- The finish-feed override.
- Reuse of the existing lead settings.
- Safe retracts between offset bands.
- The one-operation workflow.
- The separate-operation workflow for a different tool.

Update the Pocket and Contour workflow. Keep the separate rough and finish operation method for jobs that use a different tool.

## Tests

Add focused tests for these cases:

- A disabled finish sequence produces the current toolpath byte for byte.
- One finishing pass consumes the complete finish allowance.
- Two finishing passes use the expected remaining allowance.
- Spring passes repeat the final offset.
- `Stock to leave` remains after the complete sequence.
- The same formula works for Inside and Outside contours.
- Open chains use the existing air-side classification for every pass.
- Multiple rings receive every required offset band.
- Multiple Z levels receive every required offset band.
- Keep-down links do not cross between offsets.
- Every offset uses the configured lead-in and lead-out.
- A fitting failure or collision on a later pass refuses the operation.
- Tabs remain valid for every pass.
- Control and wear compensation engage and cancel for every band.
- Finish feed inherits `Feed`.
- Enabling the override copies `Feed`.
- Editing `Feed` does not change an enabled override.
- Disabling the override restores inheritance.
- Lead-in feed uses the active rough or finish feed.
- Save and load preserve every setting.
- MCP create and update preserve every setting.
- UI edits stage and undo correctly.
- Spring passes remain present after post generation.

## Done means

- 2D Contour generates optional finishing and spring passes.
- Finishing passes divide `Finish allowance` correctly.
- Spring passes repeat the final wall path.
- Existing lead-in and lead-out settings control every pass.
- Finish feed can override the operation feed.
- Spindle speed remains unchanged.
- Unsafe later passes block posting.
- Existing operations retain current behavior.
- UI, project files, undo, MCP, posting, tests and documentation agree.

body:
﻿## What happens

Importing a 3.7 MB STEP file of a twisted rotor passes the kernel import's 300 s bound and cancels. The import log line:

```
WARN camcraft_geometry::kernel_import: STEP import passed its 300s bound; cancelling
```

File: Rotor.STEP, 3,723,412 bytes, twisted rotor with curved faces. Retry gives the same result (deterministic).

## Why it matters

A user with a legitimate twisted-geometry part cannot import it at all through the STEP path - the only path for B-rep. The import does not resume or part-complete; the whole operation cancels.

## Reproduction

Import Rotor.STEP (available from the reporter) on Windows x64. The import runs the full 300 s, then the cooperative cancellation fires.

## Possible directions

- Raise or make the bound configurable is not the fix - the import is kernel-bound, single-threaded B-rep sewing. 300 s was already a generous budget.
- Profile where the kernel time goes (sewing? facetting? the fit stage of #2718/#2754?) and see whether the curved-face boundary splitting dominates.
- An interim escape: the user exports a mesh from the CAD side and imports STL/OBJ, which is fast - but loses B-rep fidelity for the fidelity checks.

Suggested labels: P3, area:geometry, effort:high, source:agent.

body:
### What happened

`stock_export.rs` states the law "a hole is a refusal": the file must not claim a solid it is not. `machined_mesh` enforces it with `iso::unpaired_edges` (#4122) on the f64 triangles. `stl_bytes` then writes each corner as `f32`. Two corners closer than one float32 step are distinct in the checked mesh and one corner in the file. Their facets are written with a repeated corner, and the edges around them are no longer on exactly two facets. The check passed, but the file is not a closed solid.

One float32 step is 7.6 um at 64 mm, 15.3 um at 150 mm and 30.5 um at 300 mm, while the marching extractor places corners anywhere along a lattice edge. On a cut stock in our lane (31.7M facets, coordinates up to about 216 mm, cell 0.254 mm), the f64 mesh had 0 open and 0 unpaired edges. The file as written had 3 edges on three or more facets and 4 facets with a repeated corner, all at one spot, with corners 4 to 9 um apart where the step is 15 um.

A related gap in `repair::weld` (`crates/geometry`) matters for any fix that welds to the written values. `drop_degenerate` keeps the first of a set of duplicate facets. A closed mesh can weld into a back-to-back pair (the same three corners, opposite windings). Each of its edges is then on two facets of the pair, so dropping only one leaves those three edges odd: the weld opens the mesh it was meant to clean.

Measured on main e6849c5ae, synthetic, through the public `stock_export::stl_bytes` and `repair::weld`:

| Input (closed in f64: 0 open, 0 unpaired) | After | open | unpaired | repeated-corner facets |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| tetrahedron near 150 mm, edge 0-1 split at a corner 3 um from corner 0 (6 facets) | `stl_bytes`, read back | 0 | 3 | 2 |
| thin tetrahedron: corners (150,150,150), (160,150,150) and two corners 3 um apart at (155,155,150) | `stl_bytes`, read back | 0 | 3 | 2 |
| the same thin tetrahedron | `repair::weld(.., 5e-6)`: kept 1, dropped 3 | 3 (`open_edge_count`) | | |

The closed answer for the thin tetrahedron is no facets at all.

### Steps to reproduce

1. The six facets: (p0, p2, a), (a, p2, p1), (p0, a, p3), (a, p1, p3), (p1, p2, p3), (p0, p3, p2), with p0 = (150, 150, 150), p1 = (160, 150, 150), p2 = (150, 160, 150), p3 = (150, 150, 160) and a = (150 + 3e-6, 150, 150).
2. `iso::unpaired_edges` is 0.
3. `stl_bytes`, then read the corners back as f32: `unpaired_edges` is 3, and 2 facets have a repeated corner.

Expected: the exported file passes the same closed check the export applied.

### Proposed fix

1. In the export, judge the mesh as it will be written. Round each corner to its `f32` value. When any facet collapses there, weld bit-exact on the rounded corners and drop the collapsed facets. Run `unpaired_edges` on that result, and write it or refuse by name. A mesh with nothing to collapse writes byte-identical to today.
2. In `repair::weld` / `drop_degenerate`, drop duplicate facets in pairs: k copies of one corner set keep k mod 2. A duplicate pair puts two uses on each of its edges, so dropping both keeps every other edge's count, and a closed mesh stays closed.

We use (1) in our own lane's writer, through `repair::weld` at 0. Pins: the two synthetic cases above (as written: closed after the fix), and a clean mesh writing byte-identical.

### Version and OS

main e6849c5ae (source build), Windows 11.

We cannot set labels. Our suggestion: `bug`, `area:sim`, `area:geometry`, `P3`.

body:
### What happened

A follow-up to #4107 / #4117 (ours). The snap in `tet` (`iso.rs`) is decided per edge: a crossing within `NODE_SNAP` of a sample, as a fraction of that edge's value span, sits on the sample. Where a floor lies on a lattice layer, the samples there read about +-1e-12 with both signs. Take a tetrahedron with two such samples `a` (inside) and `e` (outside) joined by an edge, plus one corner well inside and one well outside. The crossings on the long edges snap to `a` and to `e`. On the edge `a`-`e` both values are tiny, so its crossing stays mid-edge. The facet (`a`, crossing on `a`-`e`, `e`) has three distinct corners on one lattice edge, so its normal is exactly zero, and `push` drops it. Its three edges then lose one use each, and the mesh opens: 3 open edges per dropped facet.

Before #4117 the same facet was kept as a sliver about 1e-12 off the line. The mesh stayed closed, but the sliver counted as zero-area once the corners were welded.

Measured on main e6849c5ae, a synthetic box with its top face exactly on lattice layer 4 (step 0.25 mm). The top-layer samples are given noise of +-1e-12, both signs; every other sample is exact.

| | facets | `open_edges` | `unpaired_edges` | facets dropped with three distinct corners |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main (per-edge snap) | 2,219 | 45 | 45 | 15 |
| `NODE_SNAP` = 0 (before #4117) | 3,104 | 0 | 515 | n/a |
| per-sample snap (below) | 1,808 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

With noise of one sign only, main gives 0 / 0. Our own lane, on cut stock at cell 0.254 mm after #4117, has 39, 48 and 24 open edges on three programs, all multiples of 3.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Build a `Grid` (step 0.25, `n` = [16, 16, 8]) of a box: x and y from 0.6 to 3.4, z from 0.35 to 1.0. The top face z = 1.0 is lattice layer k = 4. On that layer, give each sample +1e-12 where (7i + 13j) mod 3 = 0 and -1e-12 elsewhere (both signs). Every other sample is the exact box distance.
2. `marching(&grid)`.
3. `open_edges` is 45. Expected: 0.

### Proposed fix

Decide the snap per sample, not per edge. In `marching`, a sample within `NODE_SNAP * step` of zero is read as +0.0: on the surface, on the outside side of `d < 0`. That sample has one value in every tetrahedron that shares it, so an edge between two such samples has no crossing and no collinear facet can arise. The per-edge test in `cross` can then go, or stay as a harmless second guard. The surface moves at most `NODE_SNAP * step` (0.25 nm at a 0.25 mm step).

Tried on a probe: the box above extracts with 0 open, 0 unpaired and no near-zero facet. The `stock_sim::iso` lib tests (7) and `stock_dual` (7) pass. Pins: the box above, and the existing #4107 pins.

### Version and OS

main e6849c5ae (source build), Windows 11.

We cannot set labels. Our suggestion: `bug`, `area:sim`, `P2` (a mesh the extractor produces fails the closed check).

title: Field engine refuses ordinary moves the column engine cuts: no caller segments a chord past the per-move ceiling

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
### What happened

`SdfField::subtract_batch` (`field_cut.rs`) refuses a chord whose clipped swept window adds more than `MAX_CELLS_PER_MOVE` (1 << 22) cells beyond the tool at rest, and the message asks the caller to segment the move. Since #4079 the module law says segmenting always brings such a chord under the ceiling.

No caller in the crate segments. `simulate_field_with` (`backend.rs`, the field arm of `Stock::simulate`) and `Stock::simulate_undercut` (`field_undercut.rs`) pass each move whole, in chunks of `BATCH_MOVES` moves. So through the public `Stock` API, the field engine refuses ordinary moves that the column engine cuts, and the program has no field result at all.

Measured on main dc3679fb5, synthetic blocks, cell 0.254 mm:

| Move | Column | Field |
|---|---|---|
| 12.7 mm flat endmill, straight X pass 5 mm deep in a 30 mm block, 50 / 100 / 150 / 200 mm | cuts | cuts |
| the same, 300 mm | cuts | refused (the ceiling) |
| 127 mm flat tool, plunge 2 / 4 mm into a 200 x 200 x 30 mm block | cuts | cuts |
| the same, plunge 6 / 10 / 20 mm | cuts | refused |
| undercut disc head 127 mm across (height 3, neck 12.7 mm), plunge 2 / 4 mm (`simulate_undercut`) | (cuts nothing, by law) | cuts |
| the same, plunge 6 / 10 / 20 mm | | refused |

The ceiling is reached by the tool's footprint times its travel, so a wide tool reaches it in a few millimetres and an ordinary endmill on a long pass. A caller that segments by a fixed length still hits it: a 5 mm plunge of the 127 mm disc adds about 4.96M cells.

We found it in our own lane, which segments every move into 5 mm pieces before `simulate_undercut`: three programs with a 127.4 mm slitting disc plunging 15 to 28 mm were refused.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `Stock::block(Backend::Field { band: FIELD_BAND }, 0.0, 0.0, 340.0, 100.0, 30.0, 0.254)`.
2. `simulate` one feed move from (20, 50, 25) to (320, 50, 25) with a flat tool of radius 6.35.
3. The field engine returns `Err` (the ceiling). The same steps on `Backend::Column` return `Ok`.

Expected: both cut. The ceiling's own answer (segmenting) is applied by the simulator, not left to every caller.

### Proposed fix

In the field arm's callers (`simulate_field_with`, `simulate_undercut`, and the lathe and display arms that chunk the same way), split a chord whose work passes the ceiling into the fewest equal pieces that bring each under it, before `subtract_batch`. `subtract_batch` keeps its refusal as the per-update bound. The work of a straight chord grows with its length, so halving converges, and the number of pieces is bounded by the move's length in cells.

Pins: the steps above cut on both engines; the 6 mm plunge of the 127 mm disc cuts through `simulate_undercut`. The existing pin `a_wide_tools_long_chord_still_refuses_and_its_segments_cut` (from #4079, ours) moves to `subtract_batch` directly, where the refusal stays.

### Version and OS

main dc3679fb5 (source build), Windows 11.

Part of #4023 and of K7 (#4027). It is delivered on `side/path-kernel` (AGENTS.md **Side branch**). It does not depend on the crate skeleton (#4055, PR #4123): it measures a finished toolpath, so it reads only the toolpath, the region and the stock.

## Why

The switch-over proof of the record `docs/decisions/4024-path-kernel-design.md` needs each law of #4023 "measured on the disc, the dog bone and `fig8.step`, old against new". The measuring code and the readings of the OLD planners can be made now. The K7 suite then runs the same measures on the new planners.

## What to do

1. Add one measuring module for tests (in the existing test helpers of `camcraft-motion`, next to `shape_mask`). For a generated toolpath it gives these readings, each as a number with the list of the places:
   - lifts on one level, and for each lift whether a named reason is given;
   - planar feeds that cross a planned cut or leave the region (a crossing);
   - entries into material: each entry with its kind, and whether it starts in air, in a hole, in a cleared column, or in solid material;
   - cuts above the engagement limit (the radial engagement against the stock that is left), with the worst value;
   - fallbacks: each note that says that a different plan was used.
2. Add a readings test for each phase-1 kind on the three parts where the kind applies, with Inside and Outside where the kind has a start side. The test pins the readings of the OLD planner as they are today (a table in the test, not a pass/fail law). A reading that breaks a law is not a failure of this issue: it is the fact that the kernel must improve. Mark each such reading in the table.
3. Use `fig8.step` only (the tracked public fixture). Never read the private project files in `testdata/models/`.
4. Keep each test under the 60 s debug budget, or use the heavy lane with a light twin by the rules.

The measuring module has unit tests on hand-made toolpaths with known readings. The readings table of the old planners is in the PR body, kind by kind, and is pinned by tests on the side branch. No planner code changes.

title: Iso-surface closed check: open_edges passes edges on four or more facets, so a zero-volume dual mesh is returned as closed

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
### What happened

`iso::open_edges` counts only edges with an odd number of facets (after its 1e-9 weld). An edge on four or six facets passes, and so does a facet whose corners meet at the weld. Two decisions read it as "the mesh is closed":

- `iso::extract_with`: a dual mesh with no open edges is returned; otherwise marching tetrahedra stand in.
- `app::stock_export` (`extract`): a mesh with open edges is refused, not written. The STL export and the stock mesh cache read it.

So a mesh that is not a valid solid can pass both.

Measured on main a1c57b475. We logged three counts at both sites: odd edges, edges on more than two facets, and facets that collapse at the weld. We ran all `camcraft-sim` tests and the `camcraft-app` suites `stock_export`, `contour_stock_run` and `stepped_stock_rapid`: 937 passed, 0 failed. 20 meshes went through the two sites:

| Site | Meshes | Odd edges > 0 | Edges on 3+ facets > 0 | Collapsed facets > 0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| dual (in `extract_with`) | 11 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| marching | 5 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `stock_export` | 4 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The one is `stock_dual::a_body_under_one_cell_never_panics_and_never_opens`. A cube 0.5 mm a side at cell 1.0 gives a dual mesh of 6 facets and volume 0. It is three flat fins: pairs of back-to-back triangles, all six on one edge. `open_edges` is 0, so `extract_with` returns it, and the test's "closed or empty" check passes. Marching tetrahedra on the same samples give 24 facets, every edge on two facets, volume 5.19e-3.

The same blind spot hid #4107: there marching tetrahedra gave 11,394 collapsed facets and 5,799 edges on three or more facets with 0 odd edges.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `let m = cube(Point3::new(0.1, 0.1, 0.1), Point3::new(0.6, 0.6, 0.6));`
2. `let f = SdfField::from_mesh(&m.facets, 1.0, FIELD_BAND).unwrap();`
3. `let tris = iso::extract_with(&f, 1.0, IsoMethod::Dual).unwrap();`
4. `iso::open_edges(&tris)` is 0. Weld on the 1e-9 lattice and count the facets on each edge: one edge is on six facets. The signed volume is 0.

Expected: a mesh that passes the closed check is a solid: every edge on exactly two facets, and no facet collapsed at the weld. Otherwise marching stands in (in `extract_with`), or the export refuses (in `stock_export`).

### Proposed fix

Add a sibling of `open_edges` that counts the edges, after the same weld, that are not on exactly two facets. A facet that collapses at the weld leaves an edge from a corner to itself, and that edge counts too. Use it at the two sites above. `open_edges` stays for its other callers.

From the measurement, the one behaviour change in the current suites is the one-cell body: its dual mesh is refused, and the closed marching mesh stands in. Pin: the steps above give a dual-method result in which every edge is on two facets (here the marching mesh), and a hand-built mesh of two cubes sharing one edge is refused by the new check while `open_edges` passes it.

### Version and OS

main a1c57b475 (source build), Windows 11.

### Labels

We cannot set labels. Our suggestion: `bug`, `area:sim`, `P3`.

- H numbers are consecutive integers from `H001`. A 3-pass cut uses `H001`, `H002`, `H003`. The operator sets their values at the control.
- The lead-in must be at least the wire radius long (the same rule as a mill cutter radius).
- `G41`/`G42` goes on the lead-in line, or on its own line immediately before the lead-in. The own-line form is easier.

The owner's example:

```
G54 G90
G29
T91
T84
T94
C001
G42 H001
G01 Y10.
X0.
G40 Y0
```

Open questions for the owner (ask before code):
- What does `G29` do on this control, and is it required?
- Which condition number goes with which pass (`C001` here, `C000` in the earlier kit)?

Work:
1. The post accepts compensation "in control" and "wear" for the LN2W dialect. It writes `G41`/`G42 Hnnn` on its own line before the lead-in, with H = pass number (from `H001`), and `G40` on the lead-out move.
2. The post refuses a lead-in shorter than the wire radius, with a message that names the operation.
3. The wire-centre path stays the default. Mark 21 output stays byte-identical.
4. Goldens for the square and the 2-axis parts with offset on, rough plus skims.

**What happens.** The rapid law in `crates/sim/src/verify/rapids.rs` (about line 112) acquits each vertical rapid that moves up. title: Field cylinder stock over ~1000 cells across builds on the column backend and is refused on the field backend (per-facet budget)

body:
### What happened

A cylinder stock wider than about 1000 cells builds on the column backend and is refused on the field backend. The field refusal is not the shared grid gate; it is the per-facet cell budget in `SdfField::from_mesh` (`field_gen.rs`, `MAX_CELLS_PER_FACET` = 1,048,576). `Stock::from_shape` meshes the cylinder with `stock_mesh` (32 segments), so each cap facet is a long thin triangle across the whole radius, and its bounding box spans millions of candidate cells.

Measured on main 3bb6647f6, cell 0.254 mm, height 1 mm:

| Diameter in cells | Column | Field |
|---|---|---|
| 4095 | builds | refused: facet 2 spans 3,306,212 candidate cells; the message asks for the mesh to be tessellated to the cell |
| 2000 | builds | refused: facet 6 spans 1,524,780 candidate cells |
| 1000 | builds | builds |
| 500 | builds | builds |

`backend.rs` says refusals are backend-independent, and names two field-only refusals (watertightness, a chord whose window spans the grid). This is a third, reached by valid stock the column arm accepts.

Found while reworking #4013 (review of the field cylinder gate).

Related (our reading of their titles, not checked against their plans): #589 and #26 retire the column engine; after that, a cylinder stock this wide would build on no backend.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `let shape = StockShape::Cylinder { diameter: 2000.0 * 0.254, height: 1.0 };`
2. `Stock::from_shape(Backend::Column, &shape, 0.254)` is `Ok`.
3. `Stock::from_shape(Backend::Field { band: 4 }, &shape, 0.254)` is `Err`, on facet 6's candidate-cell count (1,524,780), not on the grid gate.

Expected: both build, or both refuse by the same gate.

### Proposed fix

Tessellate the field cylinder's mesh to the cell before `from_mesh` (split each cap into triangles whose bounding boxes stay under the budget, as the error message itself asks), or build the cylinder's field from its exact distance instead of a mesh. A pin: a cylinder 2000 cells across builds on both backends.

### Version and OS

main 3bb6647f6 (source build), Windows 11.

We cannot set labels. Our suggestion: `bug`, `area:sim`.

title: Rotary Flow accepts a crossing between non-adjacent guide chains

labels.name: area:multiaxis
labels.description: 3+2, 5-axis, rotary

labels.name: P3

body:
The meet law of the Rotary Flow kernel checks adjacent guide pairs only. The call site is `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary_flow.rs`, in the band loop (`meet_or_cross`). A crossing between NON-adjacent guides is not checked. The kernel accepts such a set and machines it.

## Reproduction

This reproduction comes from the safety-tier review of PR #4018 (2026-11-25). Build an R8 prism with 72 sides, from Z0 to Z32. Let `d = TAU / 72`. Give the guide chains in cylindrical coordinates `(theta, Z)`:

- Guide 1: `(0, 0)` to `(0, 4)`.
- Guide 2: `(3*d, 10)` to `(3*d, 14)`.
- Guide 3: `(-d, 30)` to `(0, 2)` to `(d, 30)`.

Guide 3 crosses guide 1 at `(8, 0, 2)` in world coordinates. The kernel accepts the set on main and on the PR #4018 head. The bands that the two adjacent pairs develop cross through the same ground, and no refusal states it.

## What is wrong

A set whose guides cross non-adjacently cannot tile. The kernel blends only the adjacent pairs, so the per-pair law never reads the crossing. The user gets passes that re-machine crossed ground, with no diagnostic.

## What to do

Check every pair of picked guides for a meet or a crossing, not only the adjacent pairs. Refuse by name, at the crossing's own spot. The exact segment-pair law (Ericson 5.1) already exists in `rotary_flow_set::meet_or_cross`; extend the call to the complete set.

The workaround today: pick chains that do not cross.

This defect passes on main before PR #4018. The review of PR #4018 reported it as non-blocking and pre-existing. Issue #2829 already requests crossing-set refusals for this kernel.

The HSM Adaptive plan of one level of the user's bore can cut three times the feed length of the other plan for the same footprint. The fixture is `testdata/models/Milling-test.step` in `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs` (`the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`). The planner gives one of two plans to each level:

| Plan | Planar feeds | Arcs | Planar feed length | Feed bounding box (tool centre) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 397 | 72 | 334.31 mm | x [-7.497, 7.497], y [-7.497, 7.497] |
| B | 1933 | 918 | 999.92 mm | x [-7.491, 7.481], y [-7.344, 7.486] |

The footprint of each level is the same disc. Plan B cuts about 3 times the length of plan A. Plan B also does not reach the wall in -Y: its feeds stop 0.153 mm short of the reach of plan A. No note tells the user about the longer plan.

Measured on Linux x86_64, release, with a probe in the test (not committed):

- At 940cc5d0e (before the solidcore bump of PR #3802, mesh 6228 facets): Z 10 takes plan B. Z 15 and Z 0 take plan A. Z 5 takes a near variant of A (403 feeds, 79 arcs, 327.81 mm).
- At df899f029 and baad348f1 (after the bump, mesh 5232 facets): Z 15 and Z 5 take plan B. Z 10 and Z 0 take plan A.

The verifier finds no fault in plan B. It is not a gouge. The cost is cycle time, and a wall stock that is not even at that level.

A scout found no cap near 1000 mm or 999 arcs in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/` (`arc_proof.rs:69` prints a sum, not a limit). The spiral loop (`adaptive/core.rs:35`) and the growth loop (`adaptive/grow.rs:163`) can stop with no note.

- Find why the planner chooses plan B for some outlines of the same disc. The entry corner of the "wall corners rounded" note also changes: (5.30, -5.30) for plan B, (-5.30, -5.30) for plan A.
- Make the level plan stable for the bore, or give a note when a level plan is much longer than needed.
- Then measure the counts of `pocket3d_hsm` again and update its `BORE_PIN` with the reason.

## Notes

- Found during #3886. That issue updated the pin to the current output (4688, 4660, 1980), because the drift comes from the mesh and not from a new plan.

## What is wrong

#3537 (PR #3598) renamed the post "Agie native wire EDM" to "Native wire EDM job files". It also changed about 58 refusals from "Agie requires X" to "The native wire EDM job requires X". The wire EDM PRs of 23-25 Nov (#2955 to #2999) used the same words.

This post serves one control only. It writes AgieVision ISO, SBR and SBL job files for the AGIECUT Classic 2S. It refuses all other machines (`crates/app/src/posting_agie.rs:83`, `:88`). The generic name makes it look like a feature for all wire machines. The user cannot see that it is for the AgieVision control only.

The opposite problem also occurs, but less often. One generic wire page shows Agie text to users of all wire posts.

Examples on `origin/main` at `d80dc6944`:

- The post name: `crates/app/src/posting_agie.rs:21` `"Native wire EDM job files"`, and `assets/posts/agie-native.cps:3`.
- The `.cps` option group "Wire EDM technology" (`agie-native.cps:10`). Only this post has the option.
- About 50 refusals and UI texts, for example:
  - "The native wire EDM job requires a Wire Contour" (`operation/agie_profile.rs:28`)
  - "Native wire EDM post blocked - ..." (`posting_agie.rs:142`)
  - "A new job folder will contain the native controller files." (`ui/src/egui_app/post_dialog_tabs.rs:36`)
- The geometry crate names the post in a refusal: `crates/geometry/src/die_opening.rs:22`.
- The generic Wire page shows the hint "Agie open cuts require both clamps ..." for each open cut, for all wire posts (`ui/src/egui_app/wire_page.rs:239`). Only the AgieVision post reads the two check boxes above the hint (`agie_profile.rs:146`).

## The rule

- Use the control name only for a thing that works only for that control. The post name follows the pattern of the other wire posts, brand + process + control: "Sodick Wire EDM (Mark 21)" and "Generic ISO Wire EDM". The AgieVision post becomes "Agie Wire EDM (AgieVision)". Write "AGIECUT Classic 2S" for the machine.
- Do not use "native wire EDM", "native controller" or "the control" alone for AgieVision-only items.
- Do not put an Agie name on a generic wire EDM item. Wire Contour, DXF chain selection, arc offset, wire laws, verification, skims and DXF import are generic.
- A machine name is never a feature or an operation name. This keeps the maintainer's decision on #3537.

Decision: this rule changes the post name that #3537 chose. The rename was agreed on Discord on 25 Nov 2026, with the name "Agie Wire EDM (AgieVision)". The name keeps "Wire EDM" because Agie also builds die-sinking machines, and it matches the other wire post names.

## The classes, with examples

- **A. Agie-specific and named Agie. Keep these.**
  - Machine file `agiecut-classic-2s.mch` and model `AGIECUT CLASSIC 2S`.
  - Condition ids `AGIE_QN2` and `AGIE_BERCO_RA035`.
  - MCP tools `create_agie_inspection` and `export_agie_inspection`. CLI `export-agie-inspection`.
  - Modules `crates/post/src/agie/`, `agie_setup/`, `posting_agie.rs`, `operation/agie_profile.rs`.
  - Golden folders `golden/nc/agie-native/` and `golden/agie-setup/`. Folder `examples/agie/`.
- **B. Agie-specific but with a generic name. Rename these.**
  - Post name: "Native wire EDM job files" -> "Agie Wire EDM (AgieVision)".
  - Refusals: "The native wire EDM job requires X" -> "The Agie Wire EDM job requires X".
  - UI: "native controller files" -> "AgieVision job files (ISO, SBR, SBL)".
  - Option group: "Wire EDM technology" -> "AgieVision technology".
  - The 17 example scripts, `docs/user-guide/agie-wire-edm.md`, `site/content/guide/check-and-post/posting.md`, `site/content/guide/operations/operations-edm.md`, and the `camcraft-mcp` skill.
- **C. Generic but with an Agie name or Agie behaviour. Make these generic.**
  - The open-cut rows and hint on the Wire page (`wire_page.rs:236-240`), and the Agie inspection section and export action: #3996 shows them only for Agie jobs. This issue only renames their texts.
  - `CommandKind::ImportAgieDrawing` does a plain DXF import. Rename it to `ImportInspectionDrawing`.
  - The old-post-name alias (`LEGACY_POST`, `current_name`, `current_ref`, `current_key`) is in `posting_agie.rs`. The project loader and the commands call it. Move it to a generic alias table.
- **D. "Generic ISO".** "Generic ISO Wire EDM" (`wire-iso.cps`) is a real generic post. No Agie item has this label. Two documents are out of date:
  - `assets/posts/AGENTS.md:322` says that `wire-iso.cps` is the only wire post. It has no section for `agie-native.cps`.
  - `site/content/guide/check-and-post/machines.md:25` does not list the AgieVision post.

## Compatibility

- Keep the two old post names as hidden aliases: "Agie native wire EDM" and "Native wire EDM job files". The aliases apply to:
  - the document post and the setup post in project files;
  - the option keys `builtin:<name>`;
  - `SelectPost` and `SetSetupPost`;
  - the script `cps:` value, the MCP `post` tool and the CLI;
  - the `controller.post` value of a machine file.

- Do not change the script receipt value `"format": "Agie native wire EDM"` (`crates/app/src/script/report.rs:81`). Scripts can read it.

title: Live MCP: make the idle timeout configurable (the 5-minute drop ends a stdio client's session)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
## What happens

The app runs with `--mcp-port 7878`, and an MCP client that only launches stdio servers (Claude Code) drives it through `camcraft-cli mcp --connect 127.0.0.1:7878`.

After 300 s without a request, the app closes the client (`IDLE_TIMEOUT` in `crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs`, from #567):

```
mcp: client 127.0.0.1:53042 dropped: idle - no complete line for 300.0s; serving the next client
```

The bridge (`crates/app/src/mcp/bridge.rs`) exits when the app closes its side. The client then reports the server as disconnected, and the user has to restart it by hand. A 5-minute pause is common in a real CAM session: the user reads the agent's answer or checks the model in the window, or the agent writes notes between calls. In one session on 0.25.0 it dropped several times. The document stays open in the window, so nothing is lost, but every reconnect is manual.

## Request

Make the idle window configurable, matching `--mcp-port` / `CAMCRAFT_MCP_PORT`:

- `--mcp-idle-timeout <seconds>` and `CAMCRAFT_MCP_IDLE_TIMEOUT`
- `0` = never drop an idle client
- default stays 300 s, so #567's behaviour doesn't change

`Inbox::listen_with_idle` already takes the window, so this looks like CLI and environment plumbing only.

## Related, optional

The bridge could also reconnect on the next request instead of exiting (replaying the client's `initialize`). That would make a drop invisible to the client whatever the timeout is.

**Version:** CamCraft 0.25.0 (Arch package), Linux.

title: Research: keep face picks on a SolidCraft model after a design change, with the face names in the `.sc` model cache

body:
**What happens now**

An operation picks faces on a model. CamCraft stores each face pick as a hash of the face geometry: the plane, the outline segments, the loops and the area (`crates/geometry/src/geometry/feature.rs:880-900`, `crates/app/src/project/file.rs:756-758` on `main` `02bf65d93`).

A linked `.sc` model imports again when its file changes (#2463). Then:

- a pick on a face that did not change stays;
- a pick on a face that moved or changed size is refused at generate: "Face of 'part' is no longer in the model: re-pick it".

I saw both on 0.26.0 (2026-11-24): a top face moved from Z15 to Z17, and the operation on it needed a new pick. So each design change that touches a picked face needs a new pick by hand.

**What the `.sc` file already holds**

- SolidCraft keeps the face names of each body in the model cache. `docs/design-container.md`, section "Model cache", says that face names are recorded in the cache. The SolidCraft project has the MIT OR Apache-2.0 licence.
- In a test file in this repository, `testdata/models/solidcraft_for_beginners.sc`, the names are in `cache/model.json`, at `model.names[].faces`. An example is `"F2:side:l13"`.
- The names come from the feature history of the design. SolidCraft's own `model.faces` command gives each face its `name` and an `exact` flag. `exact: false` means that SolidCraft found the name from the geometry.
- CamCraft already reads this cache through SolidCraft's published source (`crates/kernel/src/solidcraft/cache.rs`). It reads only the final body record, not the names.

**Proposal (the need, not the code)**

- When a model comes from a `.sc` file, keep the SolidCraft face name beside each face pick.
- After the model imports again, find the face by its name first.
- The geometry still decides. If the named face is now of a different kind (for example, a plane became a cylinder), refuse as today, and give the name in the message.
- A model with no names (STEP, OBJ, STL, an older `.sc`) or a name with `exact: false`: the same behaviour as today.
- A project that does not use this does not change.

**Open questions (research before code)**

1. Do the names in `model.names[].faces` come in the same order as the faces of the body record in `cache/bodies.bin`? Does SolidCraft document this order, or is it only in its source?
2. CamCraft picks welded faces that it builds from the facets. Can each welded face keep its source face (or faces) of the body record through tessellation and welding? What happens when one welded face covers two source faces, or one source face splits into two welded faces?
3. Where does the name go:
   - on the pick in the project file, as an optional field, with or without a `PROJECT_VERSION` step;
   - or in a table on the model, which the pick refers to?
4. What does a pick do when its name is not in the new model (the face was deleted), or when two faces have the name (a split)? A proposal: refuse and give the name, as today.
5. Edges and chains: do the same with edge names (SolidCraft also names edges), or faces only at first?
6. How does this fit #3817 (advisory feature data from `document.json`)? Both read SolidCraft's published container. One reader can serve both.
7. Which tests pin it? A proposal: a pair of `.sc` fixtures (one design, before and after a dimension change), with a pick that stays by name and a pick whose face is gone.

**Who benefits**

Each user who programs a SolidCraft part and then changes the design. This includes a version-control or part-database workflow, where each new version of a part comes in as a new file. SolidCraft's RFC 0001 (`docs/rfcs/0001-craft-bridge.md`, phase 2) asks for the same result through an exchange file that does not exist yet. The `.sc` cache has the names now, so CamCraft can do this with no change in SolidCraft.

**Done means:** a research comment answers these questions, and concrete sub-issues are filed (AGENTS.md "needs-research").

I prepared this issue with Claude Code (an AI agent) and checked it.

**Prior art.** SolidCraft (Apache-2.0) has the skills `solidcraft-takeover` and `solidcraft-repro-first` in `.agents/skills/`. Use them for ideas only. Write our own text, and obey our rules (claims, "Refresh only at merge time", maintainer edits).

**Proposal.**

- `takeover` skill:
  - Do a takeover only when the author approves it, or when the claim is stale by **A claim must be live**.
  - Do not push while the author is active.
  - Push to the author's branch with maintainer edits. If GitHub refuses the push, post the patch as a comment.
  - Write one comment that names the commits and the reason.
- `repro-first` skill:
  - Reproduce the bug through MCP or a pinned test before you write the fix.
  - Record the reading from before the fix in the PR body.
  - If the bug does not reproduce on the latest `main`, stop. Post the evidence on the issue.

**Done means:** the two skills are in `.claude/skills/`, and the "How to read this file" table in `AGENTS.md` names them. The PR body has `Process change: yes`.

body:
## Problem

The GPU parity tests (`crates/gpu/tests/cut_onto.rs`, `cut_parity.rs` and others) skip by name when there is no adapter. The gate runs them without `--nocapture`, so the SKIP line is hidden. The post-merge workflow sets no `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU`. On a Linux runner with no adapter, the parity tests therefore count as a pass, and nobody sees that they did not run.

Found by the review of PR #3878 (#2629, slice S3a). On the review machine, the shared device chose the software adapter WARP, not the Intel Arc.

## Fix

- The gate counts a named GPU skip and prints it in the step summary ("SKIPPED (no adapter): <test>"). "Not run" is never a pass (AGENTS.md).
- The step report names the adapter that the tests used (hardware or software).
- Decide, and record in `docs/decisions/`, if the post-merge runner sets `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU` (it has a GPU) or stays at "skip, but report".

## Notes

- Follow-up from the review of PR #3878.

body:
Found while fixing #3744 (one ring set for Auto, Inside and Outside). Related: #3743.

## What happens

The one ring set of #3744 is the offsets of the part. At a concave place of the part, the offsets of two lobes merge. At the merge, the corner of each ring moves by more than one stepover from the corner of the next ring. Thus some cuts there take the full tool width.

Readings on `testdata/models/fig8.step` (the `offset_pass_start` heavy fixture: EM-0800-4FL, stock margin 5 mm, Outside containment):

| Pass starts at | full-width cut points (`flanks::full_width_points`) |
|---|---|
| Outside (one ring set, #3744) | 495, all at the waist band, Y 40 to 70 |
| Inside (the same ring set) | 10686 (most are the first ring along the part wall, which is named) |
| Outside before #3744 (rings parallel to the stock box) | 0 |

- The full-width cuts at the waist are not named. `level_order::full_width_at` measures the distance to the nearest cut (1.9 tool radii). The ring arms near the merge are inside that distance, so the "narrow" note does not come.
- This is a load issue, not a gouge. The gouge and crossing checks are clean on this pass.

## Expected

- The rings at a merge do not take the full tool width. One option: clean-up rings or a smaller local step between two ring corners that are more than one stepover apart (Held, "On the Computational Geometry of Pocket Machining", 1991, covers the merge of offset curves).
- A cut that still takes the full width is named on the path, by the same law that the flanks meter uses.

## Pins

- `fig8_outside_offset_cuts_no_move_at_full_width` (heavy): #3744 moved its reading from 0 to the bound "at most 520 points, all in the waist band". The fix sets it back to 0.
- A motion pin on a synthetic two-lobe part that reads the full-width points at the merge, for Inside and Outside.

Done means: the two pins are green, and no unnamed full-width cut is left at a ring merge.

title: Two sessions dispatch onto one branch: add a branch-ownership guard

labels.description: New feature or request

body:
Two sessions dispatched writers onto one branch three times tonight. The result was lost work, rejected pushes and a near force-push. The process needs an ownership guard.

## The cases

- #3567: an `issue-worker-max` held the claim from 22:14Z. A second worker (`issue-worker-high`) claimed again at 22:29Z and later pushed `e7ae538a3` to the same branch while the max worker had its own commit. The max worker's work was lost with its worktree.
- #3650: our rework worker (local `62809f42f`, on merge `68c10fc24`) and another session's implementation (`bfefff3bd` -> merge `5711344b0` -> `864897476`) diverged on `issue/2970-rotary-parallel-band`. The push would have been rejected or would have clobbered. The local design is held and recorded on the PR.
- #3577: a max-tier rework and a text-fix worker both wrote `issue/3567-ramp-entry-at-dead-end`; the text fix pushed `4d464e006` over the rework's head while the rework's independent duplicate stayed uncommitted.
- Same class, earlier: prepared branches were pushed by the coordinating session while the worker that made them was about to push (`#3391`, `#3494`).

## Harm

- A worker spends an hour, then cannot push.
- A push race invites a force-push, which the law forbids.
- Two reviews run on two implementations of one fix.
- The status reports disagree, and the coordinator relays a head that is not ours (as happened with #3650).

## Rule

Whoever claims the issue owns the branch. One writer for one branch at one time. A second session that finds a live claim or a live writer on the branch stands down and names the live writer.

## What to change

- A branch owner record that both sessions read before a dispatch: a claim comment on the PR (or the issue) that names the writer and the base, or a small `.claude/claims/issue-N` file with the writer, the branch and the head it started from.
- The coordinator checks the PR head and the owner record before every dispatch, and writes its own record.
- A push that the remote refuses because the branch moved is a STOP with a report, never a force-push.
- The skills that dispatch (`work-issue`, `review-prs`, `resolve-conflicts`, `merge-ready`) say where the record lives.

## Related

- #3567, #3577, #3650.
- The two-session setup itself: a second session and this coordinator both write the same repository.

title: 2D Chamfer: add configurable lead-in and lead-out

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## Need

2D Chamfer has no user control for lead-in or lead-out.

The operation lowers the tool at the first cut point and starts the chamfer immediately. This behavior can place the tool directly on a finished edge. It can also create visible tool marks at the start or end of a chamfer.

Open-chain support from #2988 adds a fixed air-side extension at each endpoint. That extension has no user-selected shape, length, radius, or feed behavior. It is not a complete lead feature.

Users need to:

- Start and finish a chamfer away from the final edge.
- Select a lead shape that fits the available air space.
- Use a tangential entry when a direct or perpendicular entry leaves a mark.
- Use a different lead-out when the end of the path has different clearance.
- Shorten a lead near a wall, fixture, or nearby part.
- Use the same lead concepts that 2D Contour already provides.

This issue separates three motions:

1. **Entry** moves in Z from a safe plane to the lead start.
2. **Lead-in** moves in XY and joins the chamfer path.
3. **Lead-out** moves in XY and leaves the chamfer path.

This issue adds lead-in and lead-out. It does not add ramp or helical entry.

## Current behavior

- `ChamferParams` has no lead-in or lead-out values.
- 2D Chamfer has no **Lead in / Lead out** tab.
- Closed paths enter at the selected seam and cut one circuit.
- Open paths receive fixed air-side extensions from #2988.
- The operation runs one chamfer path at one derived depth.
- The lead geometry is not persisted, exposed through MCP, or documented.

The 2D Contour lead model in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_params.rs` is useful prior art. Its `Lead` values are:

- `None`
- `Linear`
- `Arc`
- `Tangential`
- `Perpendicular`

Contour lead-fit logic also shrinks a lead when the requested shape does not fit. Chamfer needs stricter checks because the chamfer cone, not only a cutter centerline, moves through the lead.

## Proposed user interface

Show the **Lead in / Lead out** tab for 2D Chamfer.

Add these lead-in choices:

| Type | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| None | None | Start directly on the path. |
| Linear | Length | Enter behind the path tangent. |
| Arc | Radius | Join the path with a quarter arc. |
| Tangential | Radius | Join the path with a tangential semicircle. |
| Perpendicular | Length | Enter from the normal direction. |

Add these lead-out choices:

- Same as lead-in
- None
- Linear
- Arc
- Tangential
- Perpendicular

Show only the length or radius that the selected lead uses.

Use these defaults:

- Lead-in: `None`
- Lead-out: `Same as lead-in`

Old projects with no lead fields must read as `Lead::None`. A default operation must preserve the existing path.

## Motion order

The motion order for one selected chain is:

1. Rapid to the lead-start point.
2. Move in Z to the chamfer depth with the existing entry law.
3. Feed through the lead-in.
4. Cut the complete selected chamfer path.
5. Feed through the lead-out.
6. Retract to a safe plane.
7. Move to the next chain or finish the operation.

The chamfer cutting feed controls each lead feed. This issue does not add a separate lead feed.

## Closed-path rule

For a closed path:

- Lead-in starts on the air side at the selected seam.
- Lead-in joins the path at the seam.
- The operation runs the closed path once.
- Lead-out leaves from the same seam.
- The planner must prevent the lead-in and lead-out from crossing.
- The operation records the selected edge break once.

## Open-path rule

For an open chain:

- Lead-in and lead-out follow the physical air side at each endpoint.
- The planner reads the material side from the selected model.
- The planner does not infer the air side only from chain point order.
- Explicit `Side` must agree with the physical wall class.
- The fixed extension from #2988 moves under the new lead planner.
- A user selection of `None` adds no extra XY feed motion.
- A sharp turn near an endpoint must not receive an unsafe generic extension.

## Lead-fit rule

The implementation follows this order:

1. Build the requested lead.
2. Verify the complete cutter-cone sweep.
3. If the lead does not fit, halve its length or radius up to the existing lead-fit limit.
4. If a smaller lead fits, report the requested and used values in the operation notes.
5. If no safe lead fits, refuse the operation.

The operation must not silently replace an unsafe requested lead with `None`.

The refusal must name:

- The lead-in or lead-out that failed.
- The selected chain.
- The conflict location.
- The unavailable air space or material conflict.
- A useful correction, such as a shorter lead or a smaller radius.

## Cone safety rule

The lead check must verify the complete active cone envelope. It must not verify only the centerline or the virtual tip.

The check must include:

- Chamfer width.
- Cone angle.
- Tip offset from #3153.
- The full active cone band.
- The cutter body above the cone.
- The lead-to-path transition.
- The complete line or arc sweep.

A lead is legal only when that complete sweep stays on the air side and outside the model.

The generated lead must not:

- Cross selected model material.
- Enter through a finished face.
- Pass through another selected chain.
- Fold onto itself.
- Add finished geometry outside the selected edge.
- Add `EdgeBreak` credit.

## Proposed fix

1. Add persistent lead-in and lead-out values to the 2D Chamfer parameter model.
2. Reuse the existing `Lead` value family where the semantics match.
3. Add a Chamfer-specific lead planner.
4. Reuse Contour shape construction only where the mathematics match.
5. Derive the physical air side from the selected open or closed model boundary.
6. Sweep the complete cutter cone through every lead move.
7. Keep the existing Chamfer path when both leads use `None`.
8. Add the fields to project serialization and version migration.
9. Add the fields to MCP create, edit, read, and job-description output.
10. Show the controls in the 2D Chamfer **Lead in / Lead out** tab.
11. Update the operation guide and field help.

The implementation must not copy the Contour centerline room check and call it sufficient for Chamfer.

## Compatibility

- A default 2D Chamfer keeps the current closed-loop output.
- Old projects read absent lead fields as `None`.
- Old readers must reject non-default lead settings after the project-format version change.
- A `None` default must not add extra project JSON or digest bytes.
- The lead values must round-trip through project save and load.
- The lead values must round-trip through MCP.

## Related work

- #2988 and PR #3059 add selected open chains.
- #3153 adds tip offset.
- #895 models real flat, ball, or radiused chamfer-tool tips.
- #3132 and PR #3140 address a 2D Contour lead issue and remain separate.

This work must use the final chain and cone geometry from #2988 and #3153.

## Required tests

Add tests that prove:

- A closed-loop path with `None` remains unchanged.
- Missing project fields read as `None`.
- Every lead shape produces the expected geometry.
- Lead-out can differ from lead-in.
- Lead direction follows the climb direction.
- A closed path uses the correct seam for both leads.
- Open-chain leads stay on the physical air side.
- A positive tip offset remains safe through the transition.
- An inside wall does not receive an outward lead.
- A self-crossing lead is refused.
- A material-crossing lead is refused.
- A lead that can fit only when smaller is shrunk and reported.
- A lead that cannot fit is refused.
- A lead adds no `EdgeBreak` credit.
- UI values round-trip through the operation.
- Project values round-trip through save and load.
- MCP can create, edit, and read each lead value.

## Out of scope

This issue does not add:

- Ramp or helical entry.
- A separate lead feed.
- User-selected retract or pass links.
- Multiple Chamfer passes.
- Real tool-tip radius or diameter.
- Stock-to-leave or finishing stock.

## Done means

- 2D Chamfer shows lead-in and lead-out controls.
- All supported lead shapes generate deterministic motion.
- Open and closed paths use the physical air side.
- The complete cutter cone stays safe through every lead.
- Default and old projects preserve the previous path.
- No safe room produces an explicit refusal.
- Lead motion adds no `EdgeBreak` credit.
- Motion, app, UI, MCP, project, and simulation tests pass.
- The site guide describes the new controls.

Changelog: Add configurable lead-in and lead-out moves to 2D Chamfer.

title: Viewport: the thick pick-outline highlight becomes a wedge that grows to the viewport edge at a low view angle
